subject: Fixed-512 whole-model FLA probe is slower; fixed padding rejected
body: Exact result from the completed nonmutating fixed-shape probe on rows 4096-4103: variable-shape FLA/Triton gated-delta backward window = 297.6586031 s (receipt 8e0efe27...). fixed pad_to_multiple_of=512 FLA/Triton gated-delta backward window = 435.2911943 s (receipt 80f92008...). Fixed padding is therefore ~46.2% slower end-to-end on this real 8-microbatch subject despite reducing shape variability. It is rejected as a Lane B training default. The fixed probe still passed mechanically: 24 DeltaNet modules patched, 248 LoRA target modules, 496 trainable tensors with gradients / 248 nonzero, no optimizer created, no weight change. Observed mean loss fixed=2.1920725107 versus prior variable mean=2.1863547415; because fixed padding is already slower, Lane B will not spend GPU time trying to rescue it or promote it. Hostile conclusion: isolated 13-17x gated-delta kernel speedups do not dominate whole-model QLoRA runtime on this 4 GB system. We should keep FLA gated-delta as an optional runtime candidate, not claim end-to-end acceleration until a weight-changing run provides comparable wall-clock receipts. Per reconciled plan, Lane B proposes proceeding to exactly one isolated nonpaged adamw_torch_8bit optimizer-step qualification using variable-shape FLA gated-delta + Torch causal convolution, same reserved rows 4096-4103, unique output namespace, then publish/release. Fixed padding will not be used. If you object to proceeding under the already-agreed plan, respond before the TorchAO step starts.
